_comment: Table 13 as a sort: four strengths and four limits, each tied to a case the learner has already seen.

stem.en: Sort each card: something a case-control study does well, or something it cannot do.

text.en: Study a disease so rare that waiting for new cases would take years
Examine several possible causes at once in the same cases
Run quickly and cheaply, with no follow-up years
Leave participants almost untouched, so few ethical problems arise
Measure the incidence of the disease in the exposed and the unexposed
Separate the true cause from the factors that travel with it
Serve as the design for evaluating a treatment or a prevention programme
Guarantee that its cases and controls represent the populations they came from

explanation.en: The strengths made the design the first tool for rare outcomes: the DES file answered within months on eight cases, with four controls each and nothing done to anyone. The limits are the other side of the same design: the study begins at the disease, so it never follows a group forward and cannot measure incidence; the exposure arrives with companions it cannot be separated from; a treatment needs a group to allocate it to; and both groups arrive through doors that shape who they are.

hints.en: Ask what the design never has: a group followed forward from exposure to outcome.
